newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX April Brent down, falls to new six-month low.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX April Brent down, falls to new six-month low.

text.p: April Brent crude futures fell through key support on Friday in late dealings, potentially prodding the market into a lower trading range.
April Brent traded as low as $19.95 per barrel, the lowest level for the front-month contract since August 28 1996 and down 13 cents from London's settlement.
Volume on SIMEX was a modest 273 lots by 0950 GMT but brokers said the April break through $20.00 would spur bears to test further support at $19.87.
However, they said as SIMEX volume is so thin, it would take a close in London to consolidate the move below $20.00.
NYMEX crudes were down in line with the arbitrage against Brent.
April was last traded on the after-hours ACCESS system at $21.54, down 15 cents from New York.
Brokers said the EIA showed crude stocks in the U.S. fell 4.4 million barrels, bigger than the API data of 3.12 million barrels, which had kept the pressure on NYMEX.
